nodes.statement_en: A subset of a set in a power set is an element of that power set
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_2d00e1b9 {α : Type*} {x s : Set α} (h : x ⊆ s) : x ∈ 𝒫 s := by

nodes.statement_en: For any type α and any set s of elements of α, the power set 𝒫 s equals the set of all subsets t of s, i.e. 𝒫 s = {t | t ⊆ s}.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_f8727f30 {α : Type*} (s : Set α) : 𝒫 s = {t : Set α | t ⊆ s} := by

nodes.statement_en: For any type α, any predicate p on sets of elements of α, and any set t, t belongs to the set {u | p u} if and only if p t holds.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_eaf92b47 {α : Type*} (p : Set α → Prop) (t : Set α) : t ∈ {u : Set α | p u} ↔ p t := by

nodes.statement_en: If two sets A and B are equal, and an element x belongs to B, then x belongs to A.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_94a184f1 {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) (hAB : A = B) (x : α) (hx : x ∈ B) : x ∈ A := by

nodes.statement_en: if set \(A\) is a subset of set \(B\), then the power set of \(A\) is a subset of the power set of \(B\)
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_d5f96fd7 {α : Type*} (A B : Set α) (h : A ⊆ B) : 𝒫 A ⊆ 𝒫 B := by
nodes.intuition: If every element of A is also in B, then every possible subset you can make from A's elements is also a possible subset you can make from B's elements, since all of A's elements are available in B.

nodes.statement_en: For any set S and any subset X, X belongs to the power set of S if and only if X ⊆ S.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_9f349f37 (α : Type*) (S X : Set α) : X ∈ 𝒫 S ↔ X ⊆ S := by
nodes.intuition: This unfolds the definition of powerset membership, turning power-set containment into an ordinary subset statement.

nodes.statement_en: If X ⊆ A and A ⊆ B, then X ⊆ B (subset relation is transitive).
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_4dc65bb2 (α : Type*) (A B X : Set α) (h1 : X ⊆ A) (h2 : A ⊆ B) : X ⊆ B := by
nodes.intuition: Transitivity lets us chain the subset from an arbitrary element of 𝒫 A through A ⊆ B to conclude it lies in B.

nodes.statement_en: To prove that one set of sets S1 is a subset of another set of sets S2, it suffices to show that every element of S1 is an element of S2.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_15472b63 (β : Type*) (S1 S2 : Set β) (h : ∀ x, x ∈ S1 → x ∈ S2) : S1 ⊆ S2 := by
nodes.intuition: This reduces the goal 𝒫 A ⊆ 𝒫 B to a pointwise membership statement about arbitrary subsets X of A.

nodes.statement_en: If A is a subset of B, then the powerset of A is a subset of the powerset of B.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_dc8152e0 {α : Type*} {A B : Set α} (h : A ⊆ B) : 𝒫 A ⊆ 𝒫 B := by
nodes.intuition: If every element of A is in B, then every possible subset we can make from A's elements is also a possible subset we could make from B's elements, since B contains all of A's elements plus potentially more.

nodes.statement_en: For any sets x and s in a type α, x is an element of the powerset of s if and only if x is a subset of s.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_72976f28 {α : Type*} (x s : Set α) : x ∈ 𝒫 s ↔ x ⊆ s := by
nodes.intuition: This unfolds the definition of powerset membership, needed to translate between 'x ∈ 𝒫 A' and 'x ⊆ A'.

nodes.statement_en: For any sets x, A, B in a type α, if x is a subset of A and A is a subset of B, then x is a subset of B.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_2fd1c211 {α : Type*} (x A B : Set α) (h1 : x ⊆ A) (h2 : A ⊆ B) : x ⊆ B := by
nodes.lean_proof: exact LE.le.subset fun ⦃a⦄ a_1 => h2 (h1 a_1)
nodes.intuition: This is subset transitivity, used to chain x ⊆ A with the hypothesis A ⊆ B to get x ⊆ B.

nodes.statement_en: For any sets S and T of subsets of α, if every element of S is also an element of T, then S is a subset of T.
nodes.lean_statement: theorem node_dff16ae0 {α : Type*} (S T : Set (Set α)) (h : ∀ x, x ∈ S → x ∈ T) : S ⊆ T := by
nodes.intuition: This reduces proving a subset relation between collections of sets to a pointwise membership check, which is exactly how 𝒫 A ⊆ 𝒫 B will be established.
